facts.raw_span: 54-year-old woman
history of stage III invasive ductal breast carcinoma
treated with mastectomy and chemoradiation 4 years earlier
urinary frequency
worsening right-sided pelvic pain
weight loss
MRI of the pelvis showed multiple fibroids and a heterogeneous 9.4 cm lesion involving the right uterine fundus/cornua
intraoperatively, the mass was found in the right retroperitoneal space, tracking along the broad ligament and encasing the right external iliac artery
grossly, the specimen was a detached, fragmented, ill-defined mass (14 × 12 × 4 cm) with fleshy solid and cystic components, central hemorrhage, and necrosis

microscopically, the tumor invaded from the serosal surface into the myometrium and comprised sheets of small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitoses (32 per 10 high-power fields), pseudo-rosette formation, foci of cytoplasmic clearing, and necrosis
immunohistochemical stains showed diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1
immunohistochemical stains showed negativity for keratin, DOG1, synaptophysin, desmin, myogenin, WT-1, CD45, inhibin, GATA-3, and SOX-10

concepts.why: The tumor's microscopic features, including small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitoses, and pseudo-rosette formation, are consistent with Ewing's Sarcoma, which is also supported by the immunohistochemical stains showing diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1.
The tumor's location in the right uterine fundus/cornua and its invasion into the myometrium are consistent with a uterine sarcoma.

The patient's history of stage III invasive ductal breast carcinoma and the presence of a heterogeneous 9.4 cm lesion involving the right uterine fundus/cornua are consistent with metastatic breast cancer.

The tumor's microscopic features, including sheets of small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and frequent mitoses, are consistent with an undifferentiated uterine sarcoma.
The tumor's microscopic features, including invasion into the myometrium and high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, are consistent with a high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma.
The tumor's microscopic features, including small, round hyperchromatic cells and frequent mitoses, are consistent with a poorly differentiated uterine sarcoma.

rationales.F12: The immunohistochemical stains showing negativity for keratin, DOG1, synaptophysin, desmin, myogenin, WT-1, CD45, inhibin, GATA-3, and SOX-10 help to rule out other types of tumors.
